title: Nonconstant maps to integral curves give torsion-free stalk modules
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve], so $Y$ is a separated integral scheme of finite type over $k$ and dimension one, and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes whose image contains at least two points. Write $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ for the generic points (the points whose closures are the whole schemes) [def-sc-generic-point]. Then $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$ and $f(X)$ is dense in $Y$. For every $x\in X$, put $y=f(x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and let $\varphi=f_x^\sharp:A\to B$ be the induced homomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The rings $A,B$ are integral domains, $\varphi$ is injective, and $B$ is torsion free as an $A$-module for the action $a\cdot b=\varphi(a)b$: for every $a\ne0$ and $b\in B$, $\varphi(a)b=0$ implies $b=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: nonconstant implies dominant and injective stalk maps, then torsion-freeness; morphisms.tex Tag 0CC1, lemma-dominant-between-integral, (2) implies (6). Extracts former steps 1–2,5 and the torsion argument in step 6 of lem-a1-nonconstant-normal-curve-map-flat.

proof.text: By [def-pc-curve] and [def-pc-integral-scheme], both $X$ and $Y$ are nonempty irreducible schemes. Their unique generic points exist by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. The dimension in [def-pc-curve] is that of [def-pc-dimension], the supremum of the Krull dimensions of the local rings. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], the topological Krull dimension of $Y$ is therefore one.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: generic-point assertion; properties.tex Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension, equality of (1) and (2).

proof.text: Put $z=f(\eta_X)$. For every $x\in X$, continuity of the underlying map in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] gives $f(x)\in\overline{\{z\}}$, because $x\in\overline{\{\eta_X\}}$. Suppose $z\ne\eta_Y$. Then $Z=\overline{\{z\}}$ is a proper irreducible closed subset of $Y$, by uniqueness of generic points [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. If $w\in Z$ and $w\ne z$, the same uniqueness makes $\overline{\{w\}}\subsetneq Z$. Thus $\overline{\{w\}}\subsetneq Z\subsetneq Y$ would be a chain of length two, contradicting Step 1 and [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Hence $Z=\{z\}$ and $f(X)\subseteq\{z\}$, contrary to the two-point image hypothesis. Therefore $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$. Since $\eta_Y\in f(X)$ and $\overline{\{\eta_Y\}}=Y$, the image is dense.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: expand nonconstant implies dominant by the dimension-one chain argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] to $X$ and $Y$. Their generic stalks $K_X=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}$ and $K_Y=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ are fields, and all their stalks are domains with injective maps $\rho_x:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to K_X$ and $\rho_y:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to K_Y$ sending germs to generic germs. By Step 2, the generic stalk map of $f$ is a unital ring homomorphism $\alpha:K_Y\to K_X$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. It is injective: if $c\ne0$ had $\alpha(c)=0$, then $1=\alpha(cc^{-1})=0$ in the field $K_X$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof, expanded through morphisms.tex Tag 0CC1, lemma-dominant-between-integral: generic stalk fields and their embeddings.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $y=f(x)$. The square $\rho_x\circ f_x^\sharp=\alpha\circ\rho_y$ follows on each germ: represent $a\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ as $s_y$ for a section $s$ on a neighbourhood $W$ of $y$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Its pullback is $t=f_W^\sharp(s)$ on $f^{-1}W$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The left side sends $s_y$ first to $t_x$ and then to $t_{\eta_X}$; the right side sends it first to $s_{\eta_Y}$ and then to $t_{\eta_X}$. Both generic points lie in these opens by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] and Step 2. The composite $\alpha\circ\rho_y$ is injective, so $f_x^\sharp$ is injective: equality of its values implies equality after composing with $\rho_x$, and then equality of the original elements.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof; morphisms.tex Tag 0CC1, lemma-dominant-between-integral, (2) implies (6), expanded as the germ square.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\varphi=f_x^\sharp$. Step 3 gives that $A$ and $B$ are domains, and Step 4 makes $\varphi$ injective. For $a\ne0$ in $A$, injectivity gives $\varphi(a)\ne0$. Thus $\varphi(a)b=0$ in the domain $B$ forces $b=0$. With scalar action $a\cdot b=\varphi(a)b$, this is exactly the asserted torsion-free condition, for every $x$.

source.place: Tag 0CCK, lemma-flat, proof: injectivity and the domain property imply torsion-freeness.
